title: IFPA launches AI technical facility
full_text:
The Institute of Financial Professionals Australia (IFPA) has launched an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for members designed to provide them with answers to technical questions about tax and superannuation, including SMSFs.
Called Thomas, the new facility has been trained on information from the industry body’s technical materials and guidance from regulators, including the ATO, Australian Securities and Investments Commission and Australian Prudential Regulation Authority.
“Our members are busier than ever. Thomas gives them a fast, reliable starting point, with the references they need to check the answer before they act on it,” IFPA chief executive Heidi Ivory said.
The AI tool will have the ability to answer a question and provide the member with an email containing a transcript of the inquiry, additional information regarding the original request and links to sources of the information provided to assist with further review.
According to IFPA head of technical services Stuart Sheary, Thomas was not designed to replace members’ professional judgment, but rather is a tool designed to assist them to reach a well-informed answer in a more efficient manner.
Further, users of Thomas will also be able to specify the source where the AI tool searches for particular answers, including IFPA’s library, official government sources, the wider web or their own documents.
IFPA is also rolling out protection that removes important identification information in the member’s browser before a client document is uploaded.
“If members are pasting client files into a public AI tool today for technical questions, they should stop and use Thomas instead,” Ivory recommended.
IFPA currently represents a network of 22,000 members and supporters and continues to be guided by its three pillars of education, advocacy and community. The launch of its AI technical help desk, or Thomas, is designed to help members function more efficiently.
